1. `packages/react/src/experimental/SelectPanel2/__tests__/SelectPanelLoading.test.tsx` and `packages/react/src/SplitPageLayout/SplitPageLayout.test.tsx` — both files are edited in this diff (Vitest imports added, `jest.useFakeTimers()`/`jest-matchmedia-mock` removed, assertions gutted to `toBeInTheDocument()`), yet neither is added to `vitest.config.mts`'s `include` list, and their parent directories (`src/experimental/SelectPanel2/`, and `SplitPageLayout/` via the first jest.config.js hunk) are added to the Jest exclusion/ignore lists. Result: these two suites will run under neither Jest nor Vitest — silent, total loss of coverage, contradicting the PR description's claim that these two components were *not* migrated. Fix: either finish the migration and add both files to `vitest.config.mts`'s include array, or revert all changes to these two files and do not add their directories to the jest.config.js exclusion lists, so they keep running under Jest unmodified.

2. `packages/react/jest.config.js` — exclusions are added at directory granularity (`src/deprecated/UnderlineNav/`, `src/experimental/SelectPanel2/`, `src/__tests__/deprecated/`) while only one file per directory was actually migrated to Vitest. Any other test file that happens to live in those directories (now or in the future) is silently dropped from Jest with no Vitest replacement. Fix: exclude only the specific migrated file paths (or confirm via `git ls-files` that no sibling test files exist in each directory before using a directory-level pattern), not the whole directory.

3. `UnderlineNavLink.test.tsx`, `FilteredSearch.test.tsx`, `ActionList.test.tsx`, `SelectPanelLoading.test.tsx` — the `toHaveNoViolations` axe accessibility assertions are deleted in every migrated file with no Vitest equivalent added (e.g. `vitest-axe`/`jest-axe` matcher wired into `config/vitest/setup.ts`). For a design-system library, dropping a11y regression tests as a side effect of a tooling migration is a real coverage regression, not an incidental simplification. Fix: port the axe check using an equivalent Vitest matcher before merging, or explicitly confirm (and note in the PR) that equivalent a11y coverage already exists in the e2e/Playwright a11y suite for these components.

4. `packages/react/src/experimental/SelectPanel2/__tests__/SelectPanelLoading.test.tsx` — beyond point 1, the actual behavioral assertions being tested (that the live region announces the exact polite message `'test'` / `'Fetching items...'`) are replaced with a no-op `toBeInTheDocument()` check, discarding the entire point of the test. Fix: don't weaken this file's assertions in a migration PR that explicitly says this component is out of scope; if migrating, preserve the live-region message assertions using Vitest fake timers (`vi.useFakeTimers()`).

5. `packages/react/src/SplitPageLayout/SplitPageLayout.test.tsx` and its deleted `__snapshots__/SplitPageLayout.test.tsx.snap` — the snapshot assertion is replaced with a trivial `toBeInTheDocument()` check, losing real regression protection for the layout's markup, again contradicting the PR description stating this file needs "additional work." Fix: leave this file untouched per the PR's own stated scope, or properly regenerate/preserve snapshot coverage under Vitest.

6. `packages/react/src/__tests__/deprecated/ActionList.test.tsx` (`ActionList.Item` block) — `behavesAsComponent` (which exercised ref forwarding, `as` polymorphism, and `sx` prop support) is replaced by a single bare render assertion, losing contract coverage that's meaningful for a widely-reused deprecated component. Fix: add explicit assertions for ref forwarding/`as`/`sx` if those are still part of the supported API, rather than dropping the coverage entirely.

7. `packages/react/vitest.config.mts` — the three new jsdom-dependent component test files are added into the existing project block named `'@primer/react (node)'`, and `environment` is flipped from `'node'` to `'jsdom'` for that whole block, which also runs `exports.test.ts` and `storybook.test.tsx` (tests presumably written assuming a Node environment). Fix: add a separate Vitest project/config block for jsdom-based component tests (matching the existing pattern used for `Banner.test.tsx`) instead of mutating the environment of the pre-existing node project.
